contract.note: The plain reading (the paper reported substantial collapse at about 8 discs, including when the algorithm was supplied) is ordinary and fair. The AGI clause is treated as an inference, and the 1957 aside is not scored.

evidence.note: Original Apple preprint (June 7, 2025). It reports complete accuracy collapse beyond certain complexities, near-zero Hanoi results at 8 or more discs, and failure to use explicit algorithms even when they were supplied.
A rejoinder disputing how to interpret the result. It does not deny what the Apple paper reported, and it admits its own validation was preliminary.

reviews.rationale: The Apple paper reports complete accuracy collapse past certain complexities, with Hanoi near zero at about 8 discs, and says the models failed to use explicit algorithms. It also raises questions about real reasoning ability. That matches Marcus's account of what the paper showed. The rejoinder (e2) disputes the inference, not the reported findings.

contract.note: Using knowledge-heavy versus observation-heavy categories as a stand-in for familiarity is a reasonable plain reading, and the contract flags that it is indirect. 'Converging evidence' is read as consistency, not proof.

evidence.note: The original paper (June 13, 2025) reports that models do well on template-based, knowledge-heavy problems and collapse on observation-heavy problems that need new insights.
Same paper. It reports that conceptual and algorithm-logic errors dominate failures and that models handle edge cases poorly; the detailed analysis uses o3-mini.

reviews.rationale: The LiveCodeBench Pro paper reports weaker performance on problems that need new insights than on familiar template problems, and finds that conceptual reasoning errors dominate. That fits the contract's support condition. Familiarity is only measured indirectly, but the claim is only that this is converging evidence.

The directly quoted excerpt covers the o4-mini variants, and the cited table covers every model. The paper does not isolate contamination as the cause, but the claim is read as describing conditions.

reviews.rationale: The author says he wrote the rejoinder as a joke or satire, and admits it contained serious errors, including a nonsense complexity analysis and a token-formula mistake corrected in v2. That meets the contract's two requirements: humorous intent and substantive errors. His view that some criticisms were valid does not contradict this narrower claim.
